ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1.

The petitioner herein seeks for modification of award dated 31.03.2012 passed in LAQ No.6 of 2011 in respect of the land bearing Survey No.1607 of village-Gedi, Taluka: Rapar, District: Kachchh with a further prayer to direct the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada Yojana, Unit No.1,
Kanabhai Bhanubhai Bharwad vs The State Of Gujarat on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77416444/
1 respondent No.2 to pass a fresh award by making corrections and to forthwith pay the compensation to the petitioner for the land acquired by the respondent No.3 and further prayer as to hold that the petitioner is entitled to make a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
2.

Dealing with the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner to press the above noted prayers, the relevant is to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9863/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2024 undefined note that as per the contention of the petitioner he has purchased the land bearing Survey No.1607 total admeasuring 18,614 sq.meters by virtue of a registered sale deed dated 11.01.2002 by payment of due consideration to one Anduben Joga Vanol.
The further contention is that Entry No.3484 came to be mutated in the Revenue records in the name of the petitioner on 21.02.2005.

The acquisition proceedings were undertaken on the proposal submitted by the respondent No.3,
Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited for Narmada Yojana with the issuance of the Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short as "the Act' 1894") on 07.01.2011.
3.

The contention in paragraph No.3.5 of the writ petition is that without issuing any notice to the petitioner, who was the owner of the land in question, award came to be passed on 31.03.2012 and an Entry No.6996 came to be mutated in the Revenue records on 29.10.2014 depicting acquisition of the lands of the petitioner bearing Survey No.1607, which was certified on 02.12.2014.
It is then contended that in the award dated 31.03.2012, the original owner of the land, purchasers, were indicated.

The contention, thus, is that acquisition Notification was issued by the respondents without proper verification of the Revenue Records and the award, thus, records, the name of the original owners, in spite of the mutation of the name of the petitioner in the Revenue records.

4. Taking note of the above contentions, on a query made by NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9863/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2024 undefined the Court as to latches of 12 years on the part of the petitioner in approaching this Court, nothing concrete could be brought on record.

Only this much is stated that the petitioner kept on visiting office of the respondent on variouis occasions from 2012 to 2018 and on 13.06.2018, when he visited the office of the respondent No.3,
he was asked to sign a CC form, wherein the petitioner had put his thumb impression, which contains the details of his acquiring the land and the amount of compensation.
The contention is that the petitioner being an illiterate person had put his thumb impression without understanding the content of the document.
Even otherwise, the perusal of the said form would indicate that the payment was not actually made and cheque was yet to be handed over.
5. We may note that the copy of CC Form allegedly endorsed by the petitioner by putting his thumb impression has not been brought on record.
The contention of the petitioner in further paragraphs of the writ petition that he has not been paid compensation in spite of the repeated request made by him, therefore, is unbelievable.

6. As the facts of the case are not clear and the petitioner has not impleaded the original owners of the land in question/vendors in the facts of the instant petition, we do not find any good ground to entertain the prayer for modification of the award after a period of 12 years .
Reference to Section 13A of the Act, 1894 is wholly misconceived, inasmuch as, the question is about the right of Kanabhai Bhanubhai Bharwad vs The State Of Gujarat on 8 July, 2024

NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9863/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2024 undefined the petitioner to receive compensation under the award dated 31.03.2012, which as per the own case of the petitioner was published after purchase of the land in question by the petitioner.
7. In any case, the factual inquiry is not possible behind the back of the person in whose name the award has been passed.
For the above noted reasons, we do not find any merit in the petition.

8. However, the liberty is granted to the petitioner to approach the competent authority to agitate his right to receive the compensation under the award dated 31.03.2012 passed in LAQ Case No.6 of 2012.

In case the petitioner approaches the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada Yojana, Unit No.1, by moving a representation along with the copy of this order, the claim of the petitioner for disbursement of compensation under the award dated 31.03.2012 shall be duly considered, after putting notice and giving opportunity to the person in whose name compensation under the award has been disbursed.

9. The order dated 15.02.2024 passed by the Land Acquisition Officer in rejecting the application under Section 13A moved by the petitioner on the premise of the same being beyond six months, will not come in the way of the petitioner in that eventuality.

10. In any case all issues pertaining to the right, title or interest of the petitioner in the land in question shall be agitated by giving due notice and opportunity to all concerned including NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9863/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2024 undefined the persons whose name is recorded in the award.
It is further clarified that independent consideration shall be given to the claim of the petitioner and the observations made by us hereinabove will not come in the way of the petitioner.
11. With the above observations and directions, the writ petition stands disposed of.
